title: How long a step can a stock Unitree G1 or H1 take carrying lumber, and does that beat a labourer's carry rate?
summary: A model-based single-support envelope, not a walking policy: the pose just before touchdown (stance sole planted, swing sole landing L ahead and s higher, centre of mass L/2 ahead with the linear-inverted-pendulum acceleration applied as tilted gravity), solved in MuJoCo against each joint’s peak torque and a friction limit. At the stud-carry pose the G1 steps 0.70 m unloaded, 0.50 m with a 3.8 kg 2x4 (waist pitch binds) and cannot carry two; the H1 steps 0.25 m unloaded and 0.10 m with 15 kg and cannot climb a 7¾ in riser. Turned into carry rates over 5–30 m trips, a G1 delivers 0.64–1.10× a one-stud labourer and 0.16–0.27× a labourer with four studs; an H1 with 3–4 studs 0.66–1.94× and 0.16–0.48×. Labourer speed, bundle size, handling time and step time are assumed and swept. The gait is restrictive (flat soles, ZMP at the sole), so the H1 figures sit far below Unitree’s own claims; no falls, drops or energy were scored.
lede: can a stock humanoid carry a stud faster than a labourer? A MuJoCo single-support step envelope: the G1 steps 0.50 m with one 2x4 and cannot carry two; the H1 steps 0.20 m with one and 0.10 m with 15 kg; neither beats a labourer who takes a bundle of four, and the model is restrictive (no falls, drops or energy scored).
